EpicsMotor.description:
A positioner: one device, one EPICS motor record per axis.

The axes are the record names under the device's prefix
(``<experiment>:<device>:<axis>``), so the entry still carries names
only; tolerance, units and limits live in the record (``.RDBD``,
``.EGU``, ``.HLM``/``.LLM``), the one home for device facts.  Each axis
binds as a scan axis ``Device:axis`` (the same spelling as a DB
device's settable), and the device as a whole is a per-row scalar
device (every axis's readback).

kind.description: Device kind: 'epics_motor' (EPICS motor records, one per axis).
kind.title: Kind

axes.description: The axes, as the motor record names under the device's prefix (e.g. ['x', 'y', 'z'] for '<experiment>:<device>:x' …). Each is a scan axis 'Device:axis'. The record owns the axis's limits, units and deadband.

SetpointDevice.description:
A setpoint device: a supply's plain records (``NATIVE_DEVICES.md`` §8).

The entry names the records under the device's prefix
(``<experiment>:<device>:<record>``), since the worker has no DB rows to
enumerate them: each settable is its readback record, written at its
setpoint record (``<record>:SP``, or the family's setpoint role for that
readback) and confirmed on the readback within the IOC's set tolerance
(the record the family's ``tolerance_by`` role names for that setpoint);
readbacks are extra row columns; status bits are two-state records that
fail a set when they read 1. Limits, units and the set tolerance live in
the records (``DRVH``/``DRVL``, ``EGU``, ``current:TOL``), the one home
for device facts: a settable the family gives no setpoint role with a
``tolerance_by`` is refused.

kind.description: Device kind: 'setpoint_device' (a supply's plain records: setpoint, readback, status bits).
kind.title: Kind

template.description: The family file the device instantiates, one of its kind's; absent: the kind's default (REGISTRY_KIND_FAMILIES). A device also in panel_devices.yaml names the same family there. Older readers refuse the key: write it only once every reader has this schema.
template.title: Template

settables.description: The settables, by readback record name under the device's prefix (e.g. {'current': {timeout: 10}} for '<experiment>:<device>:current', written at the family's setpoint role for it, 'current:SP', and confirmed within the IOC's set tolerance, 'current:TOL'). Each must be a readback the family writes through a setpoint role with a 'tolerance_by'. Each is a scan axis 'Device:record' and a setup's set target.
settables.title: Settables

readbacks.description: Further numeric readback records, read into each row beside the settables' own (e.g. ['voltage']).
readbacks.title: Readbacks

status.description: Status bits, two-state records that read 1 when tripped (e.g. ['fault', 'interlock']): a set is refused while one reads 1 and fails if one rises while it waits.
status.title: Status

SetpointDevice.title: SetpointDevice

SetpointSettable.description:
One settable of a setpoint device: how long a scan waits for its readback.

The tolerance the readback must come within is not here: it is a device
fact the IOC holds as a record (the family's ``tolerance_by`` role for
the settable's setpoint, a supply's ``current:TOL``), read by the scan
worker at every set.  What stays is the client's patience.

``tolerance`` is the retired registry number, accepted and ignored for
one release: readers deployed before its retirement *require* it, so a
file keeps it until every reader runs this schema, and a round trip
keeps it as it was (absent stays absent, a value is written back).

tolerance.description: Retired: ignored, never a tolerance (the IOC's set-tolerance record is, read at every set). Accepted only while readers deployed before its retirement still require it; drop it from the file once every reader runs a schema that accepts its absence.
tolerance.title: Tolerance

timeout.description: Seconds the scan worker waits for the readback to arrive within the IOC's set tolerance after the write, before the set fails: the client's patience, not a device fact. Size it for the slowest ramp plus the readback's scan period. The tolerance itself is the IOC's record (the family's tolerance_by role, e.g. current:TOL), never written here.
timeout.title: Timeout

Witness.description:
A trigger domain's witness: a hardware count of its edges, the count's stamp, an epoch.

Recorded, never waited on: each strict row reads the count (the
family's ``count`` role, ``<counter>Counts``), the count record's own
timestamp and the epoch (the family's ``epoch`` role, a string that
changes whenever the count restarts). At most one witness per domain.
Names only, as every entry: the records are the family's.

kind.description: Device kind: 'witness' (a counter of a trigger domain's edges).
kind.title: Kind

template.title: Template

counter.description: The counter record's name stem under the device's prefix: the count is '<counter>Counts'. It must be the family's count record.
counter.title: Counter

domain.description: The trigger domain it counts (a plain word): the edges every synchronous device of that domain sees. One witness per domain; strict runs record the 'main' domain's.
domain.title: Domain
